info.name: account
info.description:
Every operation the service publishes, in the order the collection runner needs them.

The folders mirror the documentation pages: `Use cases` renders `docs/USE_CASES.md`, `Queries` renders `docs/QUERIES.md`, and `Health` renders `docs/HEALTH.md`. Each request keeps the name of its `operationId` summary in `openapi.yaml`, so a request and its contract are found under the same words.

Running the whole collection top to bottom works on a fresh stack. `Account opening` generates a new holder document on every run and stores the account identifier it gets back, so a second run never collides with the first.

`baseUrl` is a collection variable, so the collection runs with no environment imported. Import `account-local.postman_environment.json` to point it somewhere else.

`accountId` and `holderDocument` are runtime state, written by `Account opening` into the collection scope and, when an environment is selected, into that environment as well. A selected environment wins the lookup, so an environment left over from an earlier version of this collection carrying an empty `accountId` would shadow the value and every later request would address an empty identifier. Deleting that entry from the environment is enough, and the requests that need it stop with that reason instead of letting the service answer 404 or 422.

request.description:
Opens an account for the cardholder identified by a document number.

The document is generated before the request runs, so the collection is re-runnable. Sending the same document twice answers `409 ACCOUNT_ALREADY_EXISTS`, and a document outside 11 to 50 digits answers `422 DOCUMENT_FORMAT_NOT_VALID`.

The identifier returned here is stored in the `accountId` collection variable, which every later request reads.

request.description:
Records a transaction against the account. One endpoint serves the four operation types, and `operation_type_id` selects which one, so the saved examples carry a body each: `1` a normal purchase, `2` a purchase with installments, `3` a withdrawal, and `4` a credit voucher.

`amount` always travels positive. A credit voucher is stored positive and every other type is stored negative, which is why the balance is the plain sum of the transactions.

The body that ships is the credit voucher, because it is the only type that succeeds on its own: an account opens at a zero balance, and a debit against it answers `409 ACCOUNT_WITH_INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS`. Swap in a debit body after this request has run and the account has funds.

response.name: 409 Account with insufficient funds

query.description: Deterministic ordering, sortable by created_at and id, a leading minus marking descending. Defaults to -created_at,-id.
Items per page, 1 to 100. Defaults to 20.
Only operation_type_id is filterable, under == and =in=, with integer values. Example of the second form: operation_type_id=in=(1,2,3).
Opaque cursor of the next page, taken verbatim from links.next. Absent on the first page.

request.description:
Lists the transactions recorded against the account, most recent first.

The page is a forward-only keyset cursor, so there is no page number and no total. `links.next` carries the next cursor whenever `meta.has_next` is true, and is absent otherwise. Feed that value back into `page[cursor]` to walk the pages.

`filter` and `page[cursor]` ship disabled, so the request runs as a plain first page and both knobs stay visible.
